title: O Lord, I Call Upon You

questions.question: O Lord, I call upon you; hasten to me! Give ear to my voice when I what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:1 (ESV): "Give ear to my voice when I call to you!"

questions.question: Let my prayer be counted as incense before you, and the lifting up of my hands as the evening what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:2 (ESV): "and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice!"

questions.question: Set a guard, O Lord, over my mouth; keep watch over the door of my what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:3 (ESV): "keep watch over the door of my lips!"

questions.question: Do not let my heart incline to any evil, to busy myself with wicked deeds in company with men who work what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:4 (ESV): "in company with men who work iniquity,"

questions.question: And let me not eat of their what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:4 (ESV): "and let me not eat of their delicacies!"

questions.question: Let a righteous man strike me—it is a kindness; let him rebuke me—it is oil for my what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:5 (ESV): "let him rebuke me—it is oil for my head;"

questions.question: Let my head not refuse it. Yet my prayer is continually against their what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:5 (ESV): "Yet my prayer is continually against their evil deeds."

questions.question: When their judges are thrown over the cliff, then they shall hear my words, for they are what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:6 (ESV): "then they shall hear my words, for they are pleasant."

questions.question: But my eyes are toward you, O God, my Lord; in you I seek what?
Leave me not defenseless! Keep me from the trap that they have laid for whom?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:9 (ESV): "Keep me from the trap that they have laid for me,"

questions.question: And from the snares of evildoers! Let the wicked fall into their own what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:10 (ESV): "Let the wicked fall into their own nets,"

questions.question: As when one plows and breaks up the earth, so shall our bones be scattered at the mouth of what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:7 (ESV): "so shall our bones be scattered at the mouth of Sheol."

questions.question: Who is the author of Psalm 141?
What is compared to incense?
questions.explanation: Psalm 141:2 (ESV): "Let my prayer be counted as incense before you,"

key_verse_text: Set a guard, O Lord, over my mouth; keep watch over the door of my lips!
